structure: Cost centres in one legal entity
description: Echelon, Unbound and servicing are cost centres of one company; costs allocated for management reporting only
liability_ring_fencing: None: servicing errors, fraud losses or claims over sponsors' charitable funds reach Echelon IP and the platform business
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: Whole company inside one SOC 1/SOC 2 boundary unless carved by process; engineers who build Echelon are in scope of servicing ITGCs
licensing_polyform_nc: If the company owns the Echelon copyrights no licence is needed internally; if the copyrights sit with an individual or another entity an assignment or licence is still needed. Third-party sponsors self-hosting are a separate question (PolyForm NC permits charitable organisations)
fundraising: One cap table; investors in servicing also buy Echelon
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: No intercompany pricing; management allocations only
double_counting_risk: high: allocations are optional, so shared Echelon time is easily left out
when_appropriate: pre-revenue, before the first signed sponsor
assessment: acceptable only as a pre-revenue phase

structure: Business units in one legal entity
description: Separate P&Ls with documented internal licence and service charges (cost-plus) and metered allocation keys
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: As above; scope can be defined by process in the system description
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Internal charges mirror arm's-length terms so a later split is cheap
double_counting_risk: medium: keys and charges documented; still one legal pool
when_appropriate: from first signing until servicing liabilities or external licensees appear
assessment: recommended interim structure if a split is planned

structure: Two entities: Echelon IP company + one operating company (Unbound + servicing)
description: IP company owns Echelon components and licenses them; operating company builds Unbound and services sponsors
liability_ring_fencing: IP ring-fenced from operating liabilities; Unbound platform and servicing liabilities remain together
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: SOC 1 boundary = operating company (platform ITGCs + servicing processes); Echelon outside scope except as a software supplier
licensing_polyform_nc: Requires an executed commercial licence from the IP company (CNV-GOV-009) with escrow/fork right
fundraising: Operating company can raise; investors may demand an exclusive licence or IP assignment
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Licence of intangibles between commonly controlled parties: income should be commensurate with the income attributable to the intangible (26 U.S.C. §482); the no-markup services cost method is unavailable for services that contribute significantly to key competitive advantages (26 CFR 1.482-9(b)) [research reading, not advice]
double_counting_risk: low if the licence charge is priced and metered
when_appropriate: when external Echelon licensees are realistic
assessment: reasonable once Echelon has a second commercial user

structure: Three entities: Echelon IP co, Unbound software co, servicing co
description: Each layer is a separate company under common control with two licence/service flows
liability_ring_fencing: Strongest: servicing liabilities (instructions over charitable money, fraud, data) isolated from platform and IP
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: SOC 1 for servicing co with Unbound as a subservice organisation (inclusive or carve-out method); SOC 2 for Unbound; two examinations to coordinate
licensing_polyform_nc: Two licences (Echelon->Unbound, Unbound->servicing); servicing co buys at the same price as third-party sponsors (market comparable)
fundraising: Separate rounds possible (software vs services); more diligence cost
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Two related-party flows; documentation and benchmarking each year [research reading, not advice]
double_counting_risk: lowest (prices visible) but duplicated corporate floors (standalone vs group gap)
when_appropriate: when Unbound has external licensees and servicing has its own capital needs
assessment: premature at R; duplicated floors cost more than the ring-fence is worth before revenue

structure: Echelon IP co + Unbound co with servicing as a wholly owned subsidiary of Unbound
description: Middle ground: servicing ring-fenced as a subsidiary; consolidated reporting at Unbound
liability_ring_fencing: Servicing liabilities isolated in the subsidiary (subject to veil and contract terms)
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: SOC 1 for the subsidiary using Unbound platform controls by inclusive method; one evidence system
licensing_polyform_nc: One external licence (Echelon->Unbound); internal charge to subsidiary
fundraising: Investors fund Unbound; servicing capital via parent
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Intercompany platform charge inside a consolidated group [research reading, not advice]
when_appropriate: when the first staffed-administration sponsor signs
assessment: best fit for ring-fencing servicing without splitting the platform

structure: No servicing entity: Unbound licenses to an existing administrator who services
description: Layer C is a partner's business; Unbound earns licence revenue
assurance_scope_soc1_boundary: SOC 1 is the partner's; Unbound supplies SOC 2 and CUECs
licensing_polyform_nc: Unbound licence to partner; Echelon licence to Unbound
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Arm's-length with an unrelated party; no related-party pricing
when_appropriate: if buyers will not contract with a new servicer
assessment: economically weak: previous study partnership plan at 14 bps net never profitable within 60 months

structure: Charitable or nonprofit vehicle for servicing (to rely on PolyForm NC charitable-organisation permission)
description: Servicing performed by a nonprofit so Echelon components can be used noncommercially
liability_ring_fencing: Nonprofit governance; servicing liabilities in the nonprofit
licensing_polyform_nc: PolyForm NC permits use 'by any charitable organization ... regardless of the source of funding'; whether a nonprofit servicer qualifies is a legal question; a commercial servicer is not obviously covered
fundraising: No equity; grants or program revenue only
transfer_pricing_tax_research_level: Private-benefit and UBIT questions if a commercial affiliate profits [research reading, not advice]
assessment: not recommended without counsel; listed for completeness
